high_level_description: A Lyon Renaissance master printer compares a freshly pulled bridge woodcut with the artist’s model while its carved block and working press remain visible, a wordless hand-colored woodcut inspired by Lyon printer-gravers, with dense black cuts, pale paper, restrained indigo, madder and ochre, no writing, symbols, diagrams or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A ground-floor printing workshop in sixteenth-century Lyon with pale lime-plastered walls, dark oak ceiling beams, a tall leaded window and worn gray flagstones. Cool-neutral daylight falls across one uninterrupted workroom. The empty shell carries no lettering, numerals, insignia, wall charts, ranked documents, gates, cabinets or ceremonial architecture.

elements.desc: Oak screw printing press at the rear left, built around two upright posts, a horizontal crossbeam, iron screw, wooden platen, sliding stone bed and hinged paper frame. The frame stands open after a first pull, while the press bears no plaque, maker’s mark, number, crest, decorative seal or classification symbol.

Young pressman standing beside the press, light olive skin, short dark curls, undyed linen shirt, russet sleeveless doublet, brown hose and black shoes. With a focused sideways gaze, he holds two round black ink balls with turned wooden handles below the raised frame and waits before inking the carved block again.

Middle-aged master printer-corrector standing at center, medium-brown skin, close-cropped black hair, cream linen shirt, indigo wool gown and brown shoes. His concentrated gaze moves between the artist’s model held in his left hand and the fresh proof held in his right; he carries no key, badge, seal, measuring scale or ceremonial object.

Artist’s model drawing held vertically at the lower left, a cream sheet carrying only an ink-and-wash view of a five-arched stone bridge, an open central waterway, a gatehouse with three round windows and two small barges. The sheet has deckled edges but no signature, caption, letters, numerals, border, seal or ownership mark.

Freshly pulled woodcut proof held vertically at the lower right, a cream sheet showing the same bridge in dense black relief lines. Its central waterway is mistakenly blocked and the gatehouse has only two round windows, differences the corrector can compare directly with the five arches and three windows preserved in the artist’s model.

Rectangular hardwood relief block exposed face-up on the press bed, carved with the bridge reversed in mirror orientation. The raised lines contain the same blocked central waterway and two-window gatehouse visible on the fresh proof, showing their physical production relationship. The block carries no lettering, signature, monogram, number, decorative border or emblem.
